title.narrative: Union for Restoration - Enabling large-scale restoration through national policy in Brazil (GEF-PROVEG)

description.narrative: 1. It is envisioned that this will create increased employment and income-generating opportunities for 150,000 beneficiaries in all biomes of Brazil, thus improving their socio-economic wellbeing and resilience. Restaura Biomas will create socio-economic benefits through the following components: Component 1 - Public Policies2. This component will strengthen national and subnational frameworks to promote cross-sector coordination and enable policy implementation. With the enabling conditions in place, ecosystem restoration at scale can be achieved through public policies and instruments, such as programs, plans, incentives, and others, thus generating climate, biodiversity and social benefits. There will be public consultations and planning efforts that use community input to determine the best approaches for restoration in the project areas while supporting community needs. Component 1 also plans to support research and development initiatives, expanding the socio-economic benefits for communities in project sites. Component 2 - Networks3. Under Component 2, subnational and local interventions will help to build capacity and strengthen restoration coalitions. Capacity building and technical assistance will be used to support compliance with the Forest Code. Restaura Biomas will also support innovations in ecosystem restoration which can result in transformation impacts that generate global environmental benefits and livelihoods at the scale needed. Capacity building through technical assistance and innovation can generate increased socio-economic wellbeing for communities that depend on healthy, restored ecosystems for their livelihoods. Component 3 - Finance and Models4. Restaura Biomas plans to unlock financial flows and bridge different types of capital to support forest landscape restoration interventions led by local organizations from civil society, companies from the private sector, and governmental agencies. By creating demand for forest products and unlocking financial flows, Restaura Biomas will directly increase the economic wellbeing of communities, farmers, and businesses that depend on ecosystems for their livelihoods. 5. The 150,000 beneficiaries of the project will experience the environmental, social, and economic benefits from restoration. In particular, climate change mitigation and adaptation will support food, water, and financial security, especially for vulnerable populations. Component 4 - Monitoring & Evaluation and Knowledge Management6. The knowledge management and monitoring & evaluation products (e.g. the project website, annual progress reports, evaluations, participation in webinars and forums) can create socioeconomic benefits by sharing lessons learned and best practices for other projects that are similar in theme, scope, and/or region. By supporting best practices and learning for other projects, Restaura Biomas can indirectly improve the design and implementation of future GEF programming and other restoration projects in the region, creating environmental and social benefits for people in project areas.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
Promote structuring conditions for large-scale restoration in Brazil
